A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepEISNN framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10/100 experiments, component ablations and appendix analyses of gradients, architecture depth and feature representations.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, including event-based datasets and TinyImageNet, alongside ablations, gradient-scaling sensitivity and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The core circuit equations, dynamic initialization and E-I Prop operations are retained. However, v1 Appendix A.6.1 describes a single linear logits head, whereas v2 Appendices E.1/F.6 specify an E-I classifier without output divisive inhibition. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents an implementation change or fuller documentation.

E1.justification: Beyond retained CIFAR-10/100 coverage, v2 evaluates TinyImageNet, CIFAR10-DVS and DVS-Gesture (Table 1). This substantially broadens static image coverage and introduces event-stream object classification and gesture recognition, providing temporal-input evaluations absent from v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds BNTT, NeuNorm, TEBN, tdBN and TAB to the retained CIFAR-10 comparison, and BNTT, TEBN and TAB to CIFAR-100. These expand evaluated comparisons beyond citations in related work. Existing comparators remain; v1's SNN with default BN becomes Vanilla BN.

E3.justification: Reported CIFAR peak learning rates decrease from 0.01/0.02 to 0.001/0.002 (v1 A.6.1 versus v2 F.6). Added evaluations introduce TinyImageNet downsampling, event-data resizing and augmentation, batch size 32, and 10/16 simulation steps. Appendix F.5 adds a controlled runtime/memory protocol. These reported changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds gradient-scaling sensitivity across 1/sqrt(d), 1/d and 1/d² (Table 3), and computational-overhead analysis across five architectures (Table 4). Table 2 replaces v1's clamped Kaiming initialization of all three weight matrices with unconstrained initialization of W_EE and W_IE, changing the ablation question.

E5.justification: v1 reports point accuracies without run-count or significance information. v2 adds ± values, explicitly identifies five independent runs for starred BN/DANN reproductions, and introduces error bars and significance reporting in Figure 6. The uncertainty measure, statistical test and run count for unstarred proposed-model results remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds results including 77.66% on CIFAR10-DVS, 94.86% on DVS-Gesture and 50.29% on TinyImageNet. Retained results are revised: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 changes from 92.12% to 92.05±0.11%, and CIFAR-100 VGG-16 from 65.53% to 64.95±1.14%, with different reported settings. New sensitivity and overhead results include 2.32–2.50× training-time and 1.12–1.57× memory costs.

T1.justification: v1's current-variance and initialization-rate derivations are retained in v2 D.3/D.4. v2 additionally supplies an analytical fast-inhibitory-neuron derivation (D.1), parameter-by-parameter backpropagation formulas (D.5), and explicit moment-based initialization formulas (E.2). These substantially expand the mathematical treatment beyond relocated equations.

C1.justification: The central claim of stable, competitive normalization-free deep E-I SNN training remains. The abstract and conclusion replace explicit Dale's-law compliance with capturing cortical E-I architecture. The conclusion drops its explicit sparse-representation claim and adds a claim of compatibility with analog or mixed-signal neuromorphic platforms.

C2.justification: v2 adds digital-hardware deployment limitations and analog-platform applicability discussion (Section 6), and interprets measured computational costs as a biological-fidelity tradeoff (F.5). Appendix F.1 newly explains gradient amplification and averaging effects in different pathways. Section 5.3/F.4 also refine the distribution interpretation and soften categorical sparsity language.

D1.justification: v2 specifies convolution kernels, fan-in, classifier exceptions, first-batch initialization pseudocode, global average pooling, time-averaged logits, validation selection and no dropout (E.1/E.2/F.6). It also documents the added datasets' settings. Conversely, v1's explicit channel-normalization and direct-encoding instructions disappear. Code release remains promised upon publication.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for NeuNorm, TAB, the three added datasets and DYNAP-SE2 hardware. These extend comparison and applicability context, while the principal positioning against normalization-dependent SNNs and Cornford et al.'s E-I-constrained ANNs remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. v2 edits grammar and author information, reframes the Dale's-law subsection, and rewrites selected experimental and concluding passages. Appendix A's subsections become Appendices A–F, with implementation material regrouped and experimental details moved after supplementary results.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn, and new Figure 3 illustrates stabilization and STE. Tables 1–2 are restructured, including an ablation-component matrix, while Tables 3–4 are added. Distribution and gradient plots are revised, and the DANN comparison gains error bars and significance annotations. The feature-map example is retained as Figure 8.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support was limited to static CIFAR datasets and point comparisons. v2 substantially strengthens validation through event-based tasks, TinyImageNet, broader normalization comparisons and scaling sensitivity. Explicit computational costs and fuller implementation details also make the framework easier to assess and reproduce. Undefined statistical quantities, changed CIFAR settings and classifier ambiguity remain limitations, but the added evidence substantially improves support for the central contribution.
